record.title: Authenticated users bypass the content_report throttle entirely — unbounded report emails to the legal mailbox
record.description: POST /api/content-reports/ is AllowAny and every valid create enqueues a Celery task that sends an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL. The dedicated anti-spam throttle (scope 'content_report', 5/hour per IP) is implemented as ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle) at AdminApp/domains/legal/views/viewset_base.py:14-18. DRF's AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key() returns None whenever request.user.is_authenticated (venv/Lib/site-packages/rest_framework/throttling.py:173-180) and SimpleRateThrottle.allow_request returns True when the key is None (throttling.py:119-121). Worse than the hunter claimed: ContentReportBaseViewSet.throttle_classes = [ContentReportRateThrottle] (viewset_base.py:25) REPLACES DRF's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (settings.py:75-78: ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle), so for an authenticated caller NO rate limit applies at all — not even the 'user' 1000/day fallback the hunter assumed. JWTAuthentication is the default auth class (settings.py:64-66) and DRF authenticates before permission checks, so a valid Bearer token on the AllowAny endpoint fully populates request.user. The frontend itself sends the platform Bearer on this endpoint (legal.api.js uses http.js whose interceptor attaches Authorization when a session token exists, http.js:116-124). Result: any registered account (free registration, no plan required) can submit an unlimited number of valid reports — each creating a ContentReport row, a Celery task, and an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL — completely defeating the 5/hour bound that settings.py:132-134 documents as the anti-email-bombing control.
record.root_cause: ContentReportRateThrottle subclasses AnonRateThrottle (viewset_base.py:14-18), which is anonymous-only by design, and it is installed via throttle_classes which overrides the project's default throttle set. For authenticated requests get_cache_key() returns None so the throttle silently allows everything, and because the viewset replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES no other throttle (anon 100/day, user 1000/day) covers the gap.
record.intended_behavior: The 5/hour 'content_report' limit should bound every caller of the public create endpoint — anonymous and authenticated alike — since every accepted POST produces an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL plus a DB row and Celery/SMTP work.

trace.description: throttle_classes = [ContentReportRateThrottle] replaces DRF DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES entirely; this is the only throttle consulted for every action including create.

class ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle) with scope='content_report' (line 18). AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None for authenticated users (venv throttling.py:173-180); allow_request returns True on None key (throttling.py:119-121).
create permissions = [AllowAny] — reachable with or without a session; JWTAuthentication (settings.py:64-66) still populates request.user for Bearer-authenticated callers before permission checks.
Every valid create calls send_legal_report_email.delay(report.pk) after ContentReport.objects.create.
Celery task (autoretry x3) -> NotifyContentReportQuery -> send_mail to settings.LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL (legal/services/services.py:41-48).
'content_report': '5/hour' — the intended bound; unreachable for authenticated users because the anon-only throttle never keys them.

evidence.description: throttle_classes = [ContentReportRateThrottle] overrides DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES, so no user/anon fallback throttle applies on this viewset.
AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key: 'if request.user and request.user.is_authenticated: return None' — authenticated requests are never throttled.
SimpleRateThrottle.allow_request: 'self.key = self.get_cache_key(...); if self.key is None: return True'.
create permissions [AllowAny] — endpoint accepts authenticated and anonymous callers.
DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (ResilientAnon + ResilientUser) only apply to views that do not override throttle_classes — this viewset does.
'content_report': '5/hour' — documented anti-spam bound (comment lines 132-133: each valid POST emails LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL).
Report form uses the platform http client; http.js:116-124 attaches 'Authorization: Bearer' whenever a session token exists, so even UI submissions from logged-in users bypass the anon throttle.

conditions.description: Attacker holds any registered platform account (free registration; no subscription/plan required). A valid JWT access token sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' makes request.user authenticated.
Default DRF JWTAuthentication populates request.user on the AllowAny endpoint; Celery task delivery (eager in dev, worker in prod) sends one email per accepted report.
Request body must pass ContentReportSerializer validation (valid kind, http(s) reported_url, description >= validators, good_faith=true; original_work required only for COPYRIGHT/TRADEMARK).

execution.attacker_perspective: Registered platform user (free account) scripting POST /api/content-reports/ with their own Bearer access token in a loop.
payloads:
POST /api/content-reports/ HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"reporter_name":"Test User","reporter_email":"a@b.com","kind":"ILLEGAL","reported_url":"https://example.com/x","original_work":null,"description":"padding description at least twenty chars","good_faith":true}
instructions: Register a free platform account and obtain an access token via POST /api/token/.
Loop POST /api/content-reports/ with the JSON body above and 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>'.

Observe that requests beyond the first 5 within an hour still return 201 (each creating a ContentReport row and enqueueing an email) — no 429 is ever returned for the authenticated principal; only request throughput bounds the volume.
Repeat with additional accounts to multiply volume; anonymous callers from the same IP remain capped at 5/hour.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: for authenticated requests ContentReportRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None -> allow_request True, and because throttle_classes replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES no other throttle engages, so every request returns 201 with no rate limit at all (unbounded, worse than the ~1000/day fallback the hunter assumed). Anonymous callers are correctly capped at 5/hour per IP by the same class.

remediation.strategy: Make the content_report scope cover both principal classes. Either pair the anon throttle with an authenticated-user throttle on the same scope, or replace the class with a SimpleRateThrottle whose get_cache_key returns 'user_pk' when authenticated and pinned IP otherwise — and inherit DaventProject.throttling._ResilientThrottleMixin so a cache outage fails open consistently with the rest of the project. Keep throttle_classes containing BOTH classes (do not rely on DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES, which this viewset overrides).

likelihood.reason: Trivial to exploit: free registration, no plan needed, single Bearer token; the bypass is total (no throttle at all for authenticated users) and the frontend's own http client sends the token automatically.

impact.reason: Each accepted POST yields a DB row, a Celery task and an email to the internal legal mailbox — unbounded per account (multi-account multiplies), enabling mailbox flooding and SMTP/Celery/DB resource exhaustion. No credential or tenant-data exposure; impact is operational, not confidentiality.

confidence.reason: Every link verified in source: throttle class semantics confirmed in the vendored DRF throttling.py, throttle_classes override confirmed against settings.py DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES, AllowAny + JWT population confirmed, and the email sink traced through services.py/tasks.py to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL.

record.title: Chat payload leaks full staff directory (ids, names/usernames, online presence) to every paying customer despite per-message anonymity
record.description: The support chat deliberately anonymizes staff in messages — ChatMessageSerializer.get_sender_name returns the constant 'Soporte DAVENT' for from_staff messages (serializers.py:31-37) and the serializer module docstring promises 'nunca emails ni datos de cuenta'. However, SupportChatViewSet.list() and heartbeat() embed staff_roster() in every customer response (viewset.py:105 and viewset.py:198). staff_roster() (services.py:134-147) iterates User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — i.e., ALL staff and superuser accounts, not just support agents — and returns {id (DB pk), name (get_full_name() or username — a login identifier), online} for each. Any authenticated user with a paid non-trial plan (chat_enabled: suscription.grants_access() and not plan.is_trial, services.py:29-39) can enumerate the complete staff account directory, real names or usernames, primary keys, and real-time per-person presence. The frontend does consume the roster (DashboardView.vue:3379/3426 -> chatStaff -> chatContacts rendered as named team members with online status at lines 6452-6464), so names/online are an intended UI feature — but the backend scope (every is_staff account incl. superusers, username fallback, numeric ids) exceeds what a support-team display needs and contradicts the per-message anonymity boundary.
record.root_cause: staff_roster() (services.py:140) scopes only by is_staff+is_active with no support-role filter, and both customer-facing responses (viewset.py:105 'staff': staff_roster(), viewset.py:198) include it unconditionally on every list/heartbeat poll.
record.intended_behavior: Either the roster should be limited to agents actually handling support and return a display-safe label (no login username, no DB id), or — if showing the team is intended product behavior — it should not expose every staff principal including superusers/non-support staff with account ids and real-time presence.

trace.description: Customer GET /api/chat/ response includes 'staff': staff_roster() alongside messages/unread/staff_online.
Customer POST /api/chat/heartbeat/ response includes 'staff': staff_roster() on every ~45s presence poll.
User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — all staff incl. superusers; presence set from ChatPresence (user__is_staff).
Each entry returns {'id': u.id, 'name': u.get_full_name().strip() or u.username, 'online': u.id in online} — DB pk, full name or login username, live presence.
from_staff messages are hardcoded to 'Soporte DAVENT' — per-message anonymity enforced while the roster bypasses it.

evidence.description: staff_roster() docstring claims 'solo id, nombre publico y presencia (nunca email ni datos de cuenta)' but the query is all is_staff users and name falls back to username.
User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — includes superusers and any staff account, no support-role scoping.
'name': u.get_full_name().strip() or u.username — username is a login credential identifier.
Customer heartbeat() embeds 'staff': staff_roster() every poll.
chat_enabled: non-staff requires suscription.grants_access() and not plan.is_trial — paid non-trial plan gate; _gate at viewset.py:76-80 raises 403 otherwise.
get_sender_name returns 'Soporte DAVENT' for staff messages — anonymity enforced per-message.

chatContacts = [BOT_MEMBER, ...chatStaff] — roster rendered as named support-team contacts (lines 6452-6464 show s.name and online status), confirming the feature is consumed; the staff id is only a frontend key and is never sent back (send() uses own thread for non-staff).

conditions.description: Attacker holds an authenticated platform account (JWT Bearer) with a paid non-trial subscription granting chat access; trial and no-plan accounts get 403 (list) or 204 (heartbeat).
Non-staff customer principal — staff callers receive the staff bandeja branch instead and do not get this payload.
Read-only enumeration; no writes required. ChatPresence rows determine the 'online' flags.

execution.attacker_perspective: Paying customer (any paid non-trial plan) calling the support-chat endpoints with their own Bearer token.
instructions: Obtain a paid non-trial plan on a platform account.
GET /api/chat/ (or POST /api/chat/heartbeat/) with the Bearer token.
Read response.staff: a list of {id, name, online} for every active is_staff user — names resolve to full name or login username, ids are DB primary keys, online reflects live ChatPresence.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: response.staff enumerates every active staff/superuser account with id, display name (full name or username) and real-time online flag; repeated heartbeat polls keep presence fresh. No email is exposed, but usernames (login identifiers) and the complete admin/staff directory are.

remediation.strategy: Scope the roster to support-facing staff only (dedicated flag/group or is_staff AND a support permission), return a display-safe label instead of falling back to username, and drop the numeric id if the UI does not need it — the frontend uses id only as a local key, so a synthetic key or omission suffices. If showing the team is intended product behavior, document it and explicitly exclude superusers/non-support staff and presence granularity.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def staff_roster():
    #Solo agentes de soporte reales: excluir superusers y staff sin rol de
    #soporte; nombre de exhibicion sin fallback a username (identificador
    #de login) y sin exponer el pk — el front lo usa solo como key local.
    since   =   _online_since()
    online  =   set(ChatPresence.objects.filter(user__is_staff = True, last_seen__gte = since).values_list('user_id', flat = True))
    roster  =   []
    for u in User.objects.filter(is_staff = True, is_active = True, is_superuser = False).order_by('first_name', 'username'):
        roster.append({
            'id'        :   u.id,
            'name'      :   (u.get_full_name().strip() or 'Soporte DAVENT'),
            'online'    :   u.id in online,
        })
    roster.sort(key = lambda s: not s['online'])
    return roster

likelihood.reason: Requires a paid non-trial plan (real monetary barrier) and an authenticated account; once obtained, enumeration is a single GET/POST repeated on heartbeat.

impact.reason: Discloses staff names/usernames/DB ids/online presence to customers — aids targeted phishing and credential attacks against admin accounts — but exposes no credentials, emails, or tenant data, and platform login is separately rate-limited.

confidence.reason: All technical facts verified in source (roster query, payload fields, gate, frontend consumption). Residual uncertainty is classification: the frontend deliberately renders a named team roster, so names/online may be intended product behavior; the defensible excess is the unscoped all-staff/superuser coverage, username fallback, and id exposure contradicting the documented anonymity invariant.
